change_summary: PLOS ONE issued an expression of concern for this paper. It notes that Fig. 7 does not report the LSD1 siRNA data its text describes, and that Fig. 4 shows an apparent blot discontinuity between the 293T and A549 lanes. It also says similarities with other groups' work call the validity and provenance of the results into question, and the authors did not respond. The cell-line choice for the over-expression and knockdown experiments rests on Fig. 4, and the concern is unresolved but is not a retraction, so the findings are in doubt.
evaluation: Your draft cites Lv et al. [12] in Section 2 for higher LSD1 expression in lung cancer tissue than normal lung tissue, and the stored paper reports that finding. The notice questions the validity and provenance of the reported results in general, so it is unclear whether that tissue-expression use is touched. In Section 3 you take the H460 siRNA scratch-assay result as the clearest indication that LSD1 drives migration, the main evidence for your central hypothesis. That use is touched, because the notice says Fig. 7 does not report data for an LSD1 siRNA experiment. Overall the impact on your draft is medium.
recommendation: The notice says Fig. 7 does not report data for an LSD1 siRNA experiment, and your draft takes the H460 knockdown result as the clearest indication that LSD1 drives migration, the main evidence behind its central hypothesis. Hedge that wording in Section 3, cite the expression of concern, and don't build new work on this result without independent support. The notice also says similarities with other groups' work call the validity and provenance of the reported results into question, and your Background cites [12] for higher LSD1 expression in lung cancer tissue. Soften that sentence or add an independent source, and check the journal page in case a retraction follows.
